end.summary:
Practised showing 11–20 as one bundle of ten and loose ones.
Saanvi represented fourteen as one ten and four ones after discussion.
They represented seventeen as one ten and seven ones.
They counted the bundle as one thing once; this mix-up was corrected later in the lesson.
Teach-back was not passed; 1 of 4 attempts was unaided correct.
end.parentNote: Saanvi practised treating a bundle as ten, then counting the loose ones to make numbers such as 14 and 17. They first counted the bundle as one object, but later corrected this by saying “ten, eleven…” and identifying one ten and seven ones. At home, make a bundle of 10 pencils and add loose pencils, asking, “How many tens and how many ones?”
